spatial_entity.notes: The historical and geographic referent of Zaghāwa in early Arabic texts is not assumed to equal a modern ethnic territory, state, or later Kanem-Bornu boundary. Geometry remains unresolved.

claim.summary: Specialist scholarship on eighth-century Ibāḍī trans-Saharan slave traffic reports early Arabic testimony that Zaghāwa people were among those transported north as slaves by Berber traders. This establishes a bounded external captive-export/network-participation claim; it does not establish the prevalence of slavery within Zaghāwa territory, Kanem, Kawār, or the Bilād al-Sūdān generally.

external_participation.role_text: Documented origin population in an eighth-century trans-Saharan movement of enslaved persons; local mechanism of enslavement and territorial prevalence are not inferred.
external_participation.notes: No P-level applies to this claim. Network participation remains analytically separate from territorial practice.

source.title: Berbers and Blacks: Ibāḍī Slave Traffic in Eighth-Century North Africa
source.geographic_scope: North Africa and central trans-Saharan networks
source.independence_notes: Specialist historical analysis of Ibāḍī slave traffic drawing on early Arabic textual traditions.
source.reliability_limitations: Evidence for transport/export does not independently establish local ownership, labour regime, capture mechanism, or territorial prevalence in the southern origin region.

evidence.evidence_role: specialist synthesis of early trans-Saharan slave traffic
evidence.locator: article argument; note 23 on Zaghāwa transported as slaves

geometry.resolution_method: The source names a population/origin in a trade network but does not provide a defensible bounded territorial polygon for the claim interval. Do not substitute modern Chad/Sudan boundaries, later Kanem-Bornu extents, or a generalized Bilād al-Sūdān polygon.
